content.value_statement: Complex backend systems become hard to change when boundaries and dependencies are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through proven architecture patterns.
actual_capabilities: Compares Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Domain-Driven Design for backend systems.
Defines module boundaries, interfaces, ports, adapters, and dependency rules.
Provides migration steps for moving away from tightly coupled backend code.
Uses implementation checklists and examples from the included playbook.
Highlights durable workflow boundaries for payments and multi-step processes.
limitations: Does not validate architecture inside a running production environment.
Not suited for small localized refactors without system design impact.
Focuses on backend architecture rather than frontend interface design.
Requires domain constraints and scalability goals for specific guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Backend Service
use_cases.description: Choose an architecture pattern and define boundaries before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Growing Monolith
use_cases.description: Identify use cases, adapters, repositories, and migration steps for safer change.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Create shared rules for dependency direction, domain models, and integration boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backend context: [domain], [team size], [data complexity], [scale target]. Recommend Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, or DDD.

prompt_templates.title: Map Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these modules and workflows: [list]. Define bounded contexts, ports, adapters, repositories, and dependency rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this monolith structure: [summary]. Create phased migration steps toward the selected architecture without disrupting delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Review Workflow Resilience
prompt_templates.prompt: For this payment or fulfillment workflow: [steps]. Identify failure points, durable execution boundaries, and architecture changes that preserve domain clarity.

output_examples.input: A checkout service mixes payment calls, database writes, and email notifications in one controller.
output: Move business decisions into an order use case.
Represent payment and notification integrations as ports.
Implement Stripe and email providers as adapters.
Keep the controller limited to request and response handling.

output_examples.input: A team wants DDD guidance for customer, order, and billing workflows.
output: Define customer, ordering, and billing as separate bounded contexts.
Use aggregates for consistency rules inside each context.
Use domain events to communicate meaningful business changes.

output_examples.input: A legacy service needs a low-risk migration toward cleaner boundaries.
output: Start with one high-change workflow and extract a use case layer.
Introduce interfaces before replacing infrastructure details.
Add tests around the extracted domain behavior before wider refactoring.

best_practices: Start by defining domain boundaries, key workflows, and dependency direction.
Keep business logic independent from frameworks, databases, and transport layers.
Use small interfaces that match real use cases and are easy to test.
anti_patterns: Applying layered architecture to simple CRUD work that does not need it.
Putting business rules in controllers, database models, or framework callbacks.
Creating broad repositories or service interfaces that leak infrastructure details.

faq.question: Which architecture patterns does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and Domain-Driven Design for backend systems.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides examples and plans, but teams must adapt and test the implementation.

faq.question: Is this useful for frontend projects?
faq.answer: It is mainly useful for backend systems with domain logic and infrastructure integrations.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for small changes where architecture planning would add unnecessary complexity.

faq.question: Does it support microservice planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help identify bounded contexts and service boundaries before decomposition.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Provide domain workflows, current structure, constraints, scalability goals, and known pain points.
